Func - LV runtime error handler (Error Cluster).vi

Owning Palette: FuncVI Development

Use this VI in FuncVIs to handle errors produced by LabVIEW VIs and functions.

Details

Click the parameters for more information

 

InstanceRef is the reference to the CalcExpress instance that evaluates a CalcExpress expression.
LabVIEW error is the typical LabVIEW error cluster that should contain an error conditions returned by LabVIEW functions or VIs. If it signals an error, the VI assigns the specified error code to rtErrorCode variable within a variable context used by the calling CalcExpress instance.
status indicates error status.
code indicates error code.
source contains additional error information.
Gen CE error?. If TRUE, the VI produces a CalcExpress error if LabVIEW error code is non-zero. By default, it is FALSE.
error in specifies an error status before this VI executes. The VI runs normally only if error in is FALSE.
LV error status returns a value as the status member of LabVIEW error cluster.
dup LabVIEW error is a flow-through parameter with the same value as LabVIEW error.
LV error code returns a value as the code member of LabVIEW error cluster.
error out indicator contains TRUE if the VI puts an error description to the Error Protocol; i.e. if Gen CE error is TRUE and LabVIEW error indicates an error.  Otherwise it contains the same value as error in.

 

Func - LV runtime error handler (Error Cluster).vi - details

The VI is intended for use in FuncVIs.
The VI stores an error code, which LabVIEW VIs return, within a variable context associated with the CalcExpress instance to which InstanceRef control refers. This error code can be further evaluated in a script with the help of errno function. Review Non-Fatal runtime errors topic for details.

Typically, the VI does not produce a CalcExpress error if it obtains LabVIEW VIs error conditions. However, you can make the VI to do this if you pass TRUE to Gen CE Error control. In this case, the VI posts a description of LabVIEW error to the Error Protocol if an error occurred.

For details, see the FuncVI Development topic. Also see Example of use.
